I don't remember when exactly the term "web" fell out of favor for referring to the internet, but I can't help but think it was a mistake. When the term "internet" comes to mind, I think of massive amounts of nondescript information. Meaningless, random data. Comparatively, with the term "web" or (especially) "World Wide Web," I think less about some vast amount of vague data and more about the connection that shares and transports that data between it's organic nodes- people.

When I think about the people sharing data, and the connections between them, all of a sudden censorship efforts like the Trans-Pacific Partnership really piss me off. It's no longer the concept of some information not being able to get to where it's going. It's people not being allowed to communicate with one another. And that #TRIGGEREDs my protection instinct like no tomorrow.

I guess the heart of my thought is... I don't think censorship efforts on the internet would even get half as far as they do if we focused more on how the internet allows people to communicate with one another as opposed to focusing on what kinds of information will and won't be available.
